qt: to the Commission Irena Joveva (Renew) Subject:

In Smrekec, a village near Grosuplje in Slovenia, almost every evening for about 20 years electric cables have been burned outdoors to extract copper, along with plastic and rubber. As this is unconstitutional, the locals reported it to the police, who recorded 41 cases of incineration in 2023, 47 in 2024, 49 by September 2025 and more than 70 by September 2026. in October 2026, the National Institute for Public Health declared this ongoing practice to be a health risk, with children living in the village and in neighbouring streets being the most exposed. Over the years, the Environmental Inspectorate has carried out more than 90 procedures, but the burning continues, and in June 2026 it even withdrew the enforcement orders. Further steps also included the Ombudsman, who in January 2026 assessed the government’s response as being insufficient. 1.

How will the Commission verify that Slovenia is complying in practice with its obligations under Articles 13 and 36 of Directive 2008/98/EC, in particular as regards the protection of human health, the prevention of uncontrolled waste management and the enforcement of effective, proportionate and dissuasive sanctions?
What measures will the Commission require the Slovenian authorities to take to prevent further incineration, when fines remain unrecovered and infringements are repeated?
If systemic shortcomings are identified, will the Commission open an infringement procedure under Article 258 TFEU?
